title: Scenario A: Strong Assisting Currents (Monsoon Drift)
description: Favorable surface currents and following seas accelerate vessel progress across the Indian Ocean and European approaches.
expected_behavior: Effective SOG increases by +1.5 to +2.5 kts over commanded STW; voyage travel time is shortened by ~20-30 hours; fuel multiplier reduced.

title: Scenario B: Severe Head Currents & Headwinds
description: Persistent adverse currents and strong opposing winds confront the vessel in the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden bottlenecks.
expected_behavior: Effective SOG drops significantly below STW; travel time increases; added hydrodynamic resistance raises the fuel multiplier.

title: Scenario C: Elevated Swell & Rough Sea State
description: High seasonal swell across the Bay of Biscay and Cape approaches without crossing safety thresholds.
expected_behavior: Wave height reaches 4.5m with Sea State 6; hydrodynamic resistance factor climbs to ~1.28x; route remains feasible with navigational advisories.

title: Scenario D: Severe Cyclone / Gale Feasibility Breach
description: Severe cyclonic depression tracking across the Arabian Sea generating dangerous seas and extreme winds.
expected_behavior: Wave height reaches 7.5m, Sea State 8, storm flag active; route fails feasibility safety check with explicit safety violation codes.

title: Scenario E: Suez Headwinds vs Cape Agulhas Tail Assistance
description: Direct environmental trade-off: Suez route confronts persistent head-currents while Cape route benefits from favorable 2.2-knot Agulhas jet.
expected_behavior: Highlights contrasting environmental speed gains and added resistance between candidate routes.
